MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND
  PLANNING COMMISSION JOINT MEETING
  FEBRUARY 11, 2020

A joint adjourned meeting of the Rolling Hills Estates City Council and Planning Commission
was called to order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 5:35 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills
Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

Commission Member Present:  Carman, Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang

Commission Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Director of Community Development and Public Works David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

MAYOR SCHMITZ recessed the meeting to closed session at 5:37 p.m.

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL-ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code section 54956.9(d)(2): one potential matter

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

MAYOR SCHMITZ reconvened the meeting to open session at 5:59 p.m.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

DISCUSSION ITEM

A.  REVISIONS TO RHEMC CHAPTER 17.56 - ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS

  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton provided a brief overview of the key changes
  between the existing ordinance related to Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) and what would
  be included in the proposed new ordinance. She explained that 18 new housing-related
  bills were signed into law on 10/09/2019 which went into effect 01/01/2020. Five of these
  bills specifically address Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) and Junior Accessory Dwelling
  Units (JADUs):
  • AB 670
  • AB 68
  • AB 881
  • SB 13
  • AB 671

  She went on to explain that according to the Legislature, there is a housing crisis in regards
  to affordability and supply, and State laws have taken even more local control away due to
  the hurdles that local jurisdictions have put on the process of building ADUs and JADUs.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL/PLANNING MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 11, 2020 (ADU WORKSHOP)
   Planning Manager Naughton proceeded to outline the differences in the current ordinance,
  and the additions to the code being made in the proposed ordinance. Key changes include:

  •  Single Family Residences will be allowed one ADU + one JADU

  Planning Manager Naughton answered MAYOR SCHMITZ’s question by
  explaining that if there is one JADU on a lot and an ADU is built, the ADU
  must be detached from the home, which is what State law mandates
  according to City Attorney Don Davis.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed that this presentation is a compilation
  of the requirements within the 5 ADU-specific bills that have gone into effect.

  •  The proposed ordinance will include a new maximum size of an ADU (if all
  development standards can be met, including lot coverage) of 850 square feet for
  studio and 1 bedroom ADUs and 1,000 square feet for ADUs with more than 1
  bedroom.
  •  The current code does not have any specific criteria for the creation of JADUs. The
  new proposed ordinance would allow for the development of JADUs with a maximum
  square footage of 500 square feet, built within the existing footprint of the primary
  dwelling, and can include an expansion of up to 150 square feet to accommodate
  ingress and egress.
  •  The proposed ordinance will update the setback requirements for a detached ADU
  to allow 4 foot side and rear yard setbacks.
  •  New parking requirements will be updated to include JADUs. Exemptions will now
  include circumstances when on-street parking permits are required but not offered
  to the occupants of the ADU. Additionally, when a garage, carport, or covered
  parking structure is demolished in conjunction with the construction of an ADU or
  converted to an ADU, replacement parking will not be required.
  •  The current ordinance states that owner occupancy is required. The new laws state
  that no owner occupancy can be required from January 1, 2020 through January 1,
  2025 for ADUs, but will be required for JADUs. The proposed ordinance will include
  a requirement that deed restrictions must be recorded, stating the ADU may not be
  used for short-term rental, may not be sold separately, will be binding on successors
  and that restriction may be terminated upon removal of an ADU.
  •  New State law requires ministerial applications be processed within 60 days and this
  requirement will be reflected in the proposed ordinance. Additionally, ADUs
  proposed at the second story level will be subject to Neighborhood Compatibility
  determination by the Planning Commission.

  City Attorney Davis discussed the addition of the definition of a 2-Story ADU
  into the proposed ordinance.

  •  New laws requires that the proposed ordinance include a statement of the owner’s
  right to delay enforcement in Notice of Violations, allowing property owners to
  request a delay in code enforcement for up to 5 years under certain conditions.

  Planning Manager Naughton responded to CHAIR CARMAN’s question,
  clarifying that the delay of enforcement is only applicable to ADUs and not
  all construction projects.

  Planning Manager Naughton concluded that a draft ordinance will next be sent to the
  Department of Housing and Community Development for initial feedback. The proposed
  ordinance is scheduled to be introduced to the Planning Commission on March 2, 2020,
  and an urgency ordinance is scheduled to be introduced and adopted by the City Council
  on March 24, 2020. A regular Ordinance is scheduled to be introduced on first reading to
  the City Council March 24, 2020 and the second reading and adoption is scheduled to take
  place on April 14, 2020.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL inquired about the effect of an urgency ordinance,
  confirming that it immediately takes effect and that it will be identical to the contents of the
  regular ordinance that will follow. Planning Manager Naughton confirmed that the City must
  follow State law, which is much less restrictive, until a new ordinance is adopted.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL/PLANNING MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 11, 2020 (ADU WORKSHOP)
   VICE CHAIR RICK EDLER inquired about requirements regarding the
  removal/replacement of ADUs; if an ADU is removed, must it be replaced? City Attorney
  Davis explained that the replacement of ADUs is not a requirement within the State law.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUKERMAN began a discussion of how ADUs could potentially qualify
  under the Annual Housing Report, discussion ensued.

  COMMISSIONER TIM SCOTT asked if an ADU is required to have separate exterior
  access, which was confirmed by Planning Manager Naughton.

  Discussion ensued concerning the possibility of applications for ADUs being used as a
  pretext for simply expanding a primary dwelling, and that even if interior access doors were
  prohibited, one could unfortunately be added after the fact.

  VICE CHAIR EDLER stated that educating the public on this topic will be challenging, and
  requested a one-sheet be created for the City to use to educate residents on ADUs and
  JADUs. Planning Manager Naughton explained that part of the planning grant that will be
  coming from the State will include an outreach program, and that staff will work on outreach
  materials to use in the interim.

  COMMISSIONER YOO inquired about the option to require pre-approval from HOAs.
  Planning Manager Naughton explained that cannot be a requirement, only a suggestion,
  and that any condition in CCRs that prohibits ADUs is now null and void based on the new
  State laws. Discussion ensued regarding HOA requirements, application processing time,
  and undue delays.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUKERMAN discussed utility connections and whether or not separate
  panels or subpanels would be required.

  CHAIR CARMAN clarified the Neighborhood Compatibility review requirements, which can
  only be applied to 2-story ADUs.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL noted that ADUs cannot be built on properties that are on
  septic tanks, and must be connected to the sewer.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ summarized that there is a lot to be learned regarding ADUs, and
  thanked staff for all of their hard work on this subject.

ADJOURNMENT

At 6:51 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting to the next regular meeting of the City
Council scheduled immediately to follow at 7:00 p.m. and the next regular meeting of the
Planning Commission scheduled to be held Monday, March 2, 2020 beginning at 7:00 p.m. Both
meetings will be held in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL/PLANNING MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 11, 2020 (ADU WORKSHOP)
